incident-bot: [P1] Dedicated pool pressure alert for tenant cedarbridge (enterprise-vpc-cedarbridge). GPU util 98%, queue length 420, tail latency ~1200ms. Paging on-call.
Priya (oncall): Ack — I'm on. @Emma can you confirm customer-facing impact?
Emma (CS): CedarBridge reporting increased timeouts — ~15% errors last 6m. They opened a support call: "inference requests failing intermittently, spikes every 30s". They're in prod traffic window.
Luis (Infra): Quick summary from infra: their dedicated pool autoscaler is at max (12 nodes). There's a burst quota but policy requires Ops approval to exceed reserved capacity. We can add +4 GPUs for a short emergency burst. Est cost ~ $120/hr. Command to run: `opsctl burst-tenant cedarbridge --add 4 --duration 60m`
Priya (oncall): Can we reclaim capacity instead (throttle low-priority tenants) to avoid burst cost?
Sam (SRE): Yes — we can deprioritize non-prod and batch jobs temporarily. Example commands: `infractl set-tenant-priority --selector env!=prod low` and `infractl set-tenant-priority cedarbridge high`. Will reduce pressure within ~2m for queued non-prod.
Emma (CS): Customer asking for immediate mitigation. If Ops approves burst and we throttle non-prod, they'll accept.
Kate (Ops): Ops lead here — I approve an emergency burst but prefer limited window. Approving +4 GPUs for 45m. Kate thumbs-up :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Running: `opsctl burst-tenant cedarbridge --add 4 --duration 45m --reason "prod impact (emergency)"`
ops-bot: SUCCESS — burst applied. Provisioned 4 GPUs to cedarbridge pool. New capacity should appear in 90s.
Luis (Infra): Observability: +4 nodes came up, queue dropped from 420 -> 40 within 3m, avg latency down to ~260ms. KV cache warmed. Monitoring traces for any errors.
Priya (oncall): Good. Set 5m monitoring checks. If queue >100 after 20m, escalate to eviction plan. I'll hand off to night on-call @Jamie at 02:00 UTC once stable.
Jamie (Eng): Acknowledged handoff. I'll grab the runbook on dedicated exhaustion and keep the job prioritization in place. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-pool-exhaustion
CedarBridge-SPOC: CedarBridge — seeing marked improvement, timeouts reduced. Please keep burst active until your team confirms stability.
incident-bot: Burst expiration scheduled in 45m (will auto-deprovision). Incident ticket SILO-9876 created.
Priya (oncall): Next steps: 1) Monitor for 15m stable window then mark paging closed. 2) Work with CS to request a permanent capacity bump or relax autoscale cap for this tenant. 3) Post-incident review scheduled tomorrow.
Sam (SRE): Notes added to SILO-9876: throttled non-prod tenants for 30m, applied emergency burst +4 GPUs for 45m.
Kate (Ops): If cost approval needed for permanent change, loop in finance. For now closing active page once metrics stable for 15m.
incident-bot: Closing paging alert when monitor shows stability. Last note: preserved logs and traces under SILO-9876/cedarbridge for postmortem.
